rationale: vet-practice-verifier's scrape_website step configures fallback_url_field: 'search_results.results.0.url'. That fallback has NEVER produced a URL, and it never could: ExtractNestedField splits the path on '.' and does map access only, so when the walk reaches the '0' segment the value in hand is a []interface{}, the current.(map[string]interface{}) assertion fails, and the function returns nil. The census that found this (architecture_review/CENSUS_2026-08-07_rfc012_await_step_readers.md section 6.1) said the walk aborts at the 'results' segment; that is off by one and the correction matters to the fix, because 'results' DOES resolve - via the function's own ['response'] auto-unwrap, since the websearch adapter nests its payload under 'response' (internal/adapters/websearch/adapter.go:532). So the array-index support is needed at the segment AFTER the unwrap, not instead of it. The census has been corrected visibly rather than edited away. The defect is doubly silent, which is why it survived a bug-101 fix that wired this very key: webscrape_actions.go logs only when the fallback SUCCEEDS, and the terminal 'URL not found' error at the bottom of the resolution chain never names fallback_url_field at all, so an operator reading either surface sees no sign that a configured fallback ran and resolved to nothing. THE SCOPE CLAIM IS A QUERY, NOT AN ARGUMENT. Before submitting, live agent_definitions was censused for any dotted path carrying a numeric segment, twice, with different regexes so a strict-shape blind spot could not hide a second consumer: a strict whole-string path match and a coarse 'token.NUMBER followed by a dot or a quote' match anywhere in the config text. Both return exactly ONE row fleet-wide - vet-practice-verifier's search_results.results.0.url, the path this change exists to make resolvable. Nothing else in live config can reach the new branch. This is an ADDITIVE, OPT-IN capability in the sense OWNER RULING 2026-07-29 section 1 narrowed OUT of architecture scope: it changes no guarantee the shared mechanism makes, grants no new authority (nothing can now refute, retract or re-type anything), and is reachable by nothing until a config names a numeric segment - which today exactly one does. It cannot change the answer for any path that resolves at HEAD, because map access is tried first and unchanged, and the array branch is only reachable where the walk previously returned nil.

plan.summary: Teach ExtractNestedField to index arrays when a path segment is a bare non-negative integer, so vet-practice-verifier's fallback_url_field (search_results.results.0.url) can resolve for the first time; and stop the fallback failing silently at its only live caller. Map access stays FIRST and unchanged, so no currently-resolving path can change its answer - the array branch is reachable only where the function previously returned nil. The function had NO tests despite ~460 call sites, so the change ships with a characterisation suite that pins the existing behaviour (including that a map with a literal '0' key still wins over any index reading) before it pins the new. Live config was censused twice with different regexes: exactly one path fleet-wide can reach the new branch, and it is the one being fixed.

edits.rationale: The fix. Inside the walk loop, when the value in hand is a []interface{} and the segment is a bare, in-range, non-negative integer, index into it; otherwise return nil exactly as before. Ordering is the load-bearing detail: the slice branch is checked before the map assertion ONLY because a slice can never satisfy that assertion, so map access still wins wherever both could conceivably apply and a map carrying a literal '0' key resolves precisely as it always did. The ['response'] auto-unwrap stays map-only, unchanged. Bracket notation ('results[0].url') is deliberately NOT parsed: the config-side convention in this fleet is the bare dot segment, and bracket paths exist here only as an EMITTED convention (content_data_links.go's walker) that nothing feeds back into this resolver - adding a second accepted spelling would be inventing a vocabulary nothing asked for.

The function had NO dedicated test at all, despite roughly 460 call sites across 123 files funnelling through it - including ExtractActionInputs, through which every action's declared inputs resolve. So the characterisation half is the safety net and is written FIRST: top-level key, nested maps, the ['response'] auto-unwrap, missing key, empty path, nil map, and the case that pins the ordering guarantee (a map with a literal '0' key resolves by key, not by index). Only then the new behaviour, and the vet case is built from the websearch adapter's ACTUAL reply shape (adapter.go:532-539, elements per providers/provider.go:28-34) rather than an invented fixture, so it fails if the payload shape this fix targets is not the payload shape production sends.

The reason this survived a fix that already wired the key. The fallback branch logs ONLY on success, so 'configured, ran, resolved to nothing' is indistinguishable from 'never configured' in every log; and the terminal error at the end of the resolution chain lists url_field, url and input_data but not fallback_url_field, so even the failure message hides the dead key. One Warn on the empty branch and three words in the error string close both surfaces. This is the smallest change that would have made the original defect visible without a census.

plan.risks: WHAT COULD CHANGE FOR AN EXISTING CALLER, stated as a bound rather than a hope: nothing that resolves today can resolve differently, because the map branch is unchanged and is tried first, and the new branch is reachable only in the state where the old code had already decided to return nil (current value is a slice). The only possible behavioural delta is nil becoming a value. That is still a real delta for a caller that treats nil as 'absent' and branches on it, which is why the blast radius was measured rather than argued: live agent_definitions carries exactly ONE dotted path with a numeric segment fleet-wide (vet-practice-verifier's search_results.results.0.url), confirmed by two different regexes - a strict whole-string path match and a coarse 'token.NUMBER' match anywhere in the config text - so no other live config can reach the branch. Go-side callers pass literal paths, none of which contain a numeric segment. SCOPE DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: there are about ten other dot-path walkers in this codebase that are near-clones of this one and remain map-only (resolveFieldPath in data_helpers.go:1280 and two more copies in entity_state_actions.go:398 and workflow_actions.go:576, getFieldByPath:793, GetValueByPath:1042, FindByPath in content_search.go:29, GetValueAtExactPath in input_mapping.go:218, getNestedValueForLoop in loop_actions.go:759, getNestedValueForSpawn in spawn_group.go:409, traverseNestedPath in hitl_request_human_input.go:711, and an unexported extractNestedField dupe in multipage_actions.go:1129). Converging them is a real and separate piece of work with its own evidence burden; doing it inside this change would be exactly the bundling this lane's round 2 was rejected for. The duplication is named here so the next author finds it rather than rediscovering it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: whether the vet fallback then produces a USEFUL URL. It makes the configured path resolvable and makes its failure audible; whether the vet lane wants that specific first-result URL is that lane's call, and the new Warn is what will tell them. NOT ARCHITECTURE SCOPE, and the distinction is the one the owner drew on 2026-07-29 section 1: no guarantee of the shared mechanism changes (the guarantee is 'this walks a dotted path and returns nil when it cannot'; that still holds), no new authority, no exported symbol added or changed (ExtractNestedField already exists and its signature is untouched), no schema, no migration, no wire shape, no config vocabulary and no reserved key. The capability is inert until a config names a numeric segment. ROLLBACK is image-only and total: the previous binary reads every config this one reads, and the one path that would start resolving simply goes back to resolving to nothing.
grounded_in: The function at HEAD, platform/orchestration/datahelpers/data_helpers.go:1199, showing the map-only walk that is the whole defect: 'parts := strings.Split(fieldPath, "."); var current interface{} = data; for _, part := range parts { currentMap, ok := current.(map[string]interface{}); if !ok { return nil } ... }'

The configured value that has never resolved, docs/agent_docs/docs019_business/004_vet_practice_verifier.sql:62, scrape_website step: '"url_field": "business_record.business.website_url", "fallback_url_field": "search_results.results.0.url"'

The live row still carries it - the repo seed is history, the live row is fact. SELECT default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'scrape_website'->'config'->>'fallback_url_field' FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='vet-practice-verifier' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL; returns 'search_results.results.0.url'.

The blast-radius census, run twice with different regexes so a strict-shape blind spot could not hide a second consumer, against live agent_definitions (is_active, not a snapshot, not deleted). Strict: regexp_matches(cfg, '"([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*(\.[a-zA-Z_0-9]+)*\.[0-9]+(\.[a-zA-Z_0-9]+)*)"') returns exactly one row - vet-practice-verifier | search_results.results.0.url. Coarse: regexp_matches(cfg, '[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*\.[0-9]+(\.|")') returns exactly one row - vet-practice-verifier | 1. Both could have returned many; both returned only the path this change fixes.

CENSUS_2026-08-07_rfc012_await_step_readers.md section 6.1, the finding and the wording now corrected in place: 'vet-practice-verifier configures fallback_url_field: search_results.results.0.url, read via ExtractNestedFieldString. That function splits on . and does MAP ACCESS ONLY ... The fallback has therefore NEVER produced a URL, and it fails silently by design.' The correction recorded against it: 'off by one segment - results RESOLVES, via the function's ["response"] auto-unwrap (the websearch adapter nests its payload under response), and yields the array; it is the 0 segment where the assertion fails.'

The adapter reply shape the test fixture is built from, internal/adapters/websearch/adapter.go:532-539, which is why 'results' resolves through the unwrap and yields a []interface{} whose elements are providers.SearchResult (provider.go:28-34: title, url, snippet, published_at, source).

The sibling consumer that proves the real access pattern and that nothing else needs the index today - prepare_extraction_context.go:77-79 and :115-118 reach the array with ExtractNestedField and then index it IN GO: 'resultsPath := searchField + ".response.results" ... if resultsArr, ok := rawResults.([]interface{}); ok && len(resultsArr) > 0 { ... result["url"].(string) ... }'

The silent-failure surfaces being closed, webscrape_actions.go:230-244 (Info logged only when url != "") and the terminal error at :268-270 that never named the key: 'return nil, fmt.Errorf("URL not found - check url_field, url config, or input_data.target_url/url")'

Mutation evidence, run before submission. Removing the array branch fails exactly the seven tests that assert an indexed path resolves (VetFallbackPathResolves, LiteralZeroKeyOnMapWins on its third assertion, TrailingIndex, NestedArrays, FromRealJSON, ExtractNestedFieldString_Delegation, ExtractNestedFieldMap_OnIndexedElement) and leaves the characterisation tests green (ExistingBehaviour, ResponseUnwrapStaysMapOnly, TypedNilSliceIsNotIndexable) - which is the no-op half, the evidence that no existing behaviour was disturbed. Stated honestly: ArrayIndexEdges also stays green under that mutation, because out-of-range, negative and non-numeric segments return nil with or without the branch - that test pins the guard, not the capability, and could not have distinguished them.

Pre-existing test failures at committed HEAD, confirmed against a clean 'git archive HEAD' tree rather than attributed to this change: TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry in platform/orchestration/actions (the bugfix-136 lane's probe actions, commit ee07e3d86). Package platform/orchestration/datahelpers is 'ok' with this change applied.
